passage:
Femi: Heard the new chemistry teacher at Westbrook High started this week.
Claire: Good! Westbrook's ranked the top public high school in the state, so she's bound to be excellent. Nothing to worry about.
Femi: Malik says the first lab went fine, at least.
cue: Westbrook's ranked the top public high school in the state, so she's bound to be excellent
explanation: Claire assumes a top-ranked school means every teacher there is top-notch. A ranking reflects the school overall, and a brand-new teacher could be anywhere from great to struggling.

whyNot.fal_composition: Claire reasons from the whole school down to one teacher; composition would run the other way, from parts up to the whole.

title: The fries are great, people. Relax.
passage: Some reviewers here are complaining that the fries are soggy and bland. Come on. Halden Smash House has won Best Burger Joint in the county three years running. A place that good doesn't serve bad fries, so the complaints must be exaggerated. The double smash burger is still the best in town.
cue: A place that good doesn't serve bad fries
explanation: Dev assumes that because the restaurant as a whole is award-winning, every item it serves must be good. An award for burgers says little about the fries.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: Dev isn't generalizing from a few cases; he's pinning the whole restaurant's reputation on one item it serves.

passage: Picked up the Velta X2, and it's earned the hype: Circuit Weekly named it Phone of the Year, and the screen and speakers are excellent. A few people are griping about the selfie camera online, but if it's the best phone of the year, it has the best selfie camera of the year. Simple as that.
cue: if it's the best phone of the year, it has the best selfie camera of the year
explanation: Ollie assumes the phone's overall award applies to each feature. A phone can win on balance while one part, like the selfie camera, is only average.

whyNot.fal_composition: Ollie moves from the whole phone down to one feature; composition would go from the features up to the phone.

source: Board member Carl Hughes · Ridgeview HOA meeting
passage: I know a $1,200 special assessment for the new roof isn't welcome news, and we're offering a payment plan. But look at the numbers: Ridgeview's median household income is over $110,000, one of the highest in the county. Our residents can clearly afford this, including the folks in the Maple Court units who've been calling.
cue: Our residents can clearly afford this, including the folks in the Maple Court units
explanation: Carl uses the neighborhood's high median income to conclude every household can pay. A median says nothing about the households below it, including the Maple Court residents raising concerns.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: Carl isn't building a rule from a few cases; he applies a figure about the whole neighborhood to particular households.

title: New math program lifts district scores by six points
passage: Average math scores across the Orland district rose six points in the first year of the MathSprout program, the largest gain in a decade. Speaking to reporters, principal Grace Holloway said the result means every student at her school has benefited, and she plans to cut after-school tutoring as no longer needed.
cue: the result means every student at her school has benefited
explanation: A district-wide average can rise while some students stay flat or fall behind. Ms. Holloway treats the district's overall gain as true of each student, then cuts help some may still need.

whyNot.fal_composition: This runs from the district's overall result down to each individual student, which is division, not composition.

title: Q3 reviews: great news
passage: Team, what a quarter: our region finished at 120% of target, the best result in the company. I've completed the Q3 reviews, and I've rated all eleven of you 'exceeds expectations,' since we smashed the goal as a team. You should all be proud. Bonus letters go out Friday, and lunch is on me next week.
cue: I've rated all eleven of you 'exceeds expectations,' since we smashed the goal as a team
explanation: Renata treats the region's total as proof that every rep performed well. A team can beat its target thanks to a few big sellers while others fall short.

whyNot.fal_composition: Renata reasons from the team's result down to each member, not from members up to the team, so it's division rather than composition.

title: Pull all of this week's muffins
passage: Our flour supplier just recalled lot 4471 because it may be contaminated with E. coli. I checked the logs: every muffin we've baked since Monday used flour from that lot. So every one of this week's muffins is covered by the recall, including the ones already wrapped for the café. Please pull them all and set them aside for disposal.
cue: every muffin we've baked since Monday used flour from that lot
explanation: The recall covers the whole lot, and Hector confirms each muffin was made from it. A risk that applies to all of the flour does carry down to each muffin made with it.

whyNot.fal_division: The recall applies to all the flour in the lot, so every muffin made from it is covered; here the trait genuinely transfers to each part.

passage:
Aiko: The movers chipped Grandma's blue vase. Is it covered?
Ken: Her collection is insured under one policy, and the policy schedule lists every item individually, the vase included, at appraised value.
Aiko: So the vase itself is covered, not just the collection overall. I'll file the claim tonight.
cue: the policy schedule lists every item individually, the vase included
explanation: Aiko isn't assuming the vase is covered just because the collection is. The policy lists each item individually, so the coverage really does apply to the vase itself.

whyNot.fal_division: The coverage is written to apply to each listed item, so concluding the vase is covered follows from the policy, not just from the whole.
